correctness.rationale: For α>−1 set β=α+1,s=r² and s∈(1/(α+2),2/(α+3)). Harmonic Fourier basis has circle trace diagonal d_n=2π r(1−s)^β s^n (α+2)_n/n!, with decreasing consecutive ratios and strictly isolated double maximum d_1 at n=±1. Ellipses remain in a compact subdisk, making the trace form a compact self-adjoint operator-norm analytic family; Kato finite-eigenspace reduction applies. First-order 2×2 effective matrix is d1[[0,2−L/2],[2−L/2,0]], L=1+2βs/(1−s), giving |3−(2α+5)s| |ε|/[2(1−s)]. Cancellation occurs exactly at s*=3/(2α+5). Fourier selection then yields diagonal second-order direct q and only n=3 complement coupling x=s²(β+2)(β+3)/6; total q=(β−3)(2β+3)/(4β(5β+9))=((α−2)(2α+5))/(4(α+1)(5α+14)). At β=3,s=1/3 the quadratic term vanishes; third-order direct off-diagonal 17/8 and indirect paths −25/16 sum to 9/16. Odd parity removes diagonal third-order and the top eigenvalue produces 1+(9/16)|ε|³+O(ε4). Signs are consistent under ellipse rotation ε→−ε. These are operator-optimal not finite-mode-only asymptotics.
